title: An element of IB, B integral over A, is a root of a monic polynomial with non-leading coefficients in I
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a ring map of commutative rings with $B$ integral over $A$, let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal and let $z\in IB$ (the ideal of $B$ generated by the image of $I$). Then there is a monic polynomial $g=x^d+\sum_{j<d}a_jx^j\in A[x]$ with $g(z)=0$ in $B$ and $a_j\in I$ for all $j<d$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00H5 (lemma-integral-integral-over-ideal: every element of IS is integral over I) with Definition Tag 00H2 (definition-integral-over-ideal, coefficients $a_j\in I^{d-j}$; here only $a_j\in I$ is stated, which follows since $I^{d-j}\subseteq I$ for $j<d$); the form used in More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 09XG
